steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sawm (fasting) during Ramadan is the third Pillar of Islam. Muslims do not eat, drink, smoke or engage in sexual activity from dawn (Fajr) to sunset (Maghrib) for the entire month of Ramadan — the month when the Qur'an was first revealed to Muhammad.

steps.title: RS Exam Tips — Sawm: Fasting
steps.body: 1. For Sawm: Fasting questions, always include specific scriptural or source references where relevant 2. Explain both religious and non-religious viewpoints 3. Use specialist vocabulary precisely (e.g. terms from the specification) 4. Evaluate by analysing strengths and weaknesses of different views before reaching your conclusion 5. Link your discussion of Sawm: Fasting to its real-world impact on believers and society

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: In the UK, summer Ramadan fasting days can last over 18 hours, from approximately 2:30am to 9:30pm. Despite this extreme challenge, surveys show that over 90% of British Muslims fast during Ramadan, with many reporting that the spiritual benefits far outweigh the physical difficulty.

steps.title: UK Context
steps.body: During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, British Muslims faced the unusual challenge of fasting during Ramadan while mosques were closed. Communities adapted by organising virtual iftars, online tarawih prayers and contactless food distribution to those in need, demonstrating how the spirit of Ramadan could be maintained even under extreme restrictions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two reasons why Muslims fast during Ramadan.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always refer to specific sources of authority (scripture, sacred texts, religious leaders) Explain contrasting beliefs — different views within and between traditions Use key terminology precisely (e.g. tawhid, atonement, sanctity of life) For 12-mark evaluation questions, consider both sides before reaching a justified conclusion Link beliefs to their impact on individuals, communities and society Acknowledge diversity — no religious tradition has a single, uniform view
